history.summary: THIS IS A SANAMAHI SHRINE OF THE TRADITIONAL MEITEI RELIGION, NOT A HINDU TEMPLE — keep-or-drop decision needed. The Pakhangba Temple (Iputhou Pakhangba Laishang) stands beside the Nungseng Eekon, to the left of the Kangla Sanathong (western gate) inside Kangla Fort, Imphal West. This 48-ft structure in Meitei architecture was built by the Manipur Police Housing Corporation under the Kangla Fort Board between December 2008 and January 2010, and consecrated on 19 February 2010 by maibas and maibis who invoked God Pakhangba at Nungjeng Pukhri Macha, with a Hiyang Hiren (royal boat) installed alongside; the maibi procession with pena music was led by the then state health minister. Its features are the sacred altar to God Pakhangba and the seven-coloured flag-designed roof symbolizing the seven Meitei clans. The reconstruction fulfilled a long-cherished public desire after a century of neglect. It is visited by Sanamahi followers and non-followers alike; Princess Maha Chakri Sirindhorn of Thailand visited during the Sangai festival in November 2018. town_description: Imphal is the capital of Manipur, set in the flat Imphal Valley at about 786 m and ringed by hills. It is the historic seat of the Meitei kings — Kangla Fort, the former royal palace and the Govindajee temple stand at its centre — and the heart of Manipuri Vaishnavite culture, classical dance and handloom. The city is Manipur's road and air hub, served by Bir Tikendrajit International Airport and national highways to Nagaland, Assam and Myanmar.
